audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ModExp gas calculation safe from integer overflow?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: ModExp gas calculation must be safe from integer overflow in all arithmetic operations
boundary_conditions: max(base_length, modulus_length) up to uint32 max

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Uses bits.Mul64 for safe multiplication with overflow detection
key_observations: modExpMultComplexityEip7883 uses uint64 for return, uint32 input - no overflow possible
bits.Mul64 returns (hi, lo) allowing overflow detection via gasHi != 0 check
Returns math.MaxUint64 on overflow instead of wrapping
EIP-7823 caps input lengths to 1024 in Osaka fork

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Implementation uses bits.Mul64 for safe multiplication (line 536-537) and checks gasHi != 0 for overflow. Input validation caps lengths to 1024 bytes under EIP-7823 (Osaka fork). Integer types are correctly sized: uint32 inputs, uint64 outputs.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are EIP-7825 and EIP-7883 activated simultaneously at Fusaka fork?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: EIP-7825 (TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT) and EIP-7883 (ModExp gas) must be activated at the same fork

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Both EIPs gated by isOsaka() check
key_observations: Both use same fork activation condition

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Both EIP-7825 and EIP-7883 are gated by the same IsOsaka/isOsaka() fork condition. PrecompiledContractsOsaka uses osaka:true flag, and txpool uses isEIP7825 := p.isOsaka(). Fork activation is atomic.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do MEV-Boost relays validate gas cap for submitted blocks?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: MEV-Boost relays should validate EIP-7825 gas cap

key_observations: MEV-Boost relay validation is external software
Erigon validates at block import via state_transition.go:342

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: MEV-Boost relay implementations are external to Erigon. The EL client validates gas limits during block validation at core/state_transition.go:342. Relay validation is the responsibility of relay operators.
phase3_formal_audit_result.recommendation: Verify relay implementations separately. Erigon's block validation provides defense-in-depth.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation catch private channel txpool bypasses?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Block validation must enforce gas cap regardless of transaction source
boundary_conditions: All transaction sources including private channels

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Gas cap validated in state transition preCheck
key_observations: Check occurs in preCheck() called during TransitionDb()
Validation happens at execution time, not at txpool entry
Blocks containing oversized transactions will fail validation

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Gas cap is validated during block execution in state_transition.go:341-344. This check applies to ALL transactions regardless of how they entered the block (txpool, private channel, builder). Returns ErrGasLimitTooHigh if exceeded.

audit_items.title: Verify Pre-Condition: Is ceiling division used in multiplication_complexity for words?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Word count must use ceiling division: words = ceil(x/8)

key_observations: Addition of 7 before division implements ceiling

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Implementation at line 421 uses numWords := (uint64(x) + 7) / 8, which correctly computes ceiling division. For x=33: (33+7)/8=5, for x=40: (40+7)/8=5, for x=41: (41+7)/8=6. Matches EIP-2565 specification.

audit_items.title: Verify Post-Condition: Is iteration_count = bit_length(exponent) - 1 for small non-zero exponents?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: For non-zero exponents, iteration_count = max(bit_length - 1, 0)

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Line 530: expHeadBits := max(expBitWidth, 1) - 1 correctly implements iteration_count. For exp=1 (bitLen=1): max(1,1)-1=0. For exp=2 (bitLen=2): max(2,1)-1=1. Matches EIP specification.

audit_items.title: Verify Post-Condition: Is bit_length of top 32 bytes computed correctly for large exponents?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: bit_length must count significant bits in top 32 bytes of exponent

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Iterates bytes, uses bits.LeadingZeros8 for first non-zero
key_observations: expHeadLen := min(expLen, 32) - correctly limits to 32 bytes
Iterates through expHeadExplicitBytes finding first non-zero
Handles leading zeros correctly by skipping them

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Lines 522-529 correctly compute bit_length: iterates bytes, skips leading zeros, computes position of highest set bit using bits.LeadingZeros8. Formula accounts for byte position and bit position within byte.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: Is ModExp gas computation using only integer arithmetic (no floating-point)?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: All ModExp gas calculations must use integer arithmetic for determinism

key_observations: All variables are uint64 or uint32
No float64 or float32 types used

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Code review confirms all arithmetic uses uint64/uint32 types. No float/double imports or casts. Division is integer division. bits.Mul64 provides deterministic 128-bit multiplication result as two uint64 values.

audit_items.title: Verify Pre-Condition: Is gas cap check on raw tx.gasLimit, not derived values?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Gas cap must be checked on raw gasLimit field before any transformation

key_observations: st.msg.Gas() returns the raw gas limit from transaction

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Both state_transition.go:342 and pool.go:1064 check raw gas value directly. st.msg.Gas() returns the transaction's gas field without transformation. MaxTxnGasLimit = 16,777,216 is compared directly.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: Is ModExp gas cost monotonically non-decreasing with input size?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Gas cost must be monotonically non-decreasing as input sizes increase

key_observations: EIP-2565: words^2 where words = ceil(x/8) - strictly increasing
words^2 is monotonic for positive words
potential_issues: EIP-7883 has discontinuity at x=32 but both sides are >=16

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Both formulas are monotonically non-decreasing. For EIP-7883: at x=32, cost=16; at x=33, words=ceil(33/8)=5, cost=2*25=50>16. The quadratic formula ensures costs increase with input size.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: Is EIP-7883 gas cost >= EIP-2565 gas cost for all inputs?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: EIP-7883 must not reduce gas costs below EIP-2565 for any input

key_observations: For x>32: EIP-7883 = 2 * EIP-2565, clearly >= EIP-2565
minGas increased from 200 to 500 in Osaka

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: For x>32: EIP-7883 = 2*EIP-2565, always greater. For x<=32: EIP-7883=16, EIP-2565=ceil(x/8)^2<=16. Additionally, minGas increased 200->500. No regression possible.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ECDSA signature recovery correctly deriving sender addresses?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: ECDSA signature recovery must correctly derive sender address from signature

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Implementation follows Ethereum Yellow Paper Appendix F. Signature validation checks r,s bounds and v values. Public key recovery via secp256k1. Address = last 20 bytes of keccak256(pubkey[1:]).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the ECDSA r-component range validation enforced?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: ECDSA r-component must satisfy 0 < r < secp256k1N

key_observations: Line 286-288: if r.IsZero() || s.IsZero() return false

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: TransactionSignatureIsValid checks r.IsZero() (line 286) and r.Lt(secp256k1N) (line 297). Combined, this enforces 0 < r < SECP256K1N as required by the specification.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-2 low-s normalization enforced?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: ECDSA s-component must satisfy s <= secp256k1N/2 (EIP-2)

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: EIP-2 enforcement at crypto.go:291-294. When homestead=true (all post-Homestead chains), allowPreEip2s=false, enforcing s <= secp256k1N/2. This prevents transaction malleability.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are transaction type signing hashes non-colliding?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Different transaction types must have non-colliding signing hashes

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Type prefix in signing hash computation
key_observations: Legacy: RLP without prefix or with chainId in V
Type prefixes don't overlap with valid RLP first bytes

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Each typed transaction includes its type byte (0x01-0x04) in the signing hash computation. These prefixes are < 0x80 and don't overlap with valid RLP encoding of legacy transactions (which start >= 0xc0 for lists).

audit_items.title: Verify Conditional Scope: Pre-EIP-155 cross-chain replay vulnerability awareness

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Pre-EIP-155 transactions (v=27,28) allow cross-chain replay by design

key_observations: signChainID set to nil for unprotected
potential_issues: Known design limitation, not a bug

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Pre-EIP-155 transactions are still accepted (sg.unprotected=true in signers). This is a known design limitation, not a Fusaka-specific issue. No changes in Fusaka affect this behavior.
phase3_formal_audit_result.recommendation: Document as known limitation. Users should always use EIP-155 protected transactions.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does snapshot mechanism provide true deep-copy isolation?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: State snapshots must provide complete isolation via deep copy

key_observations: Erigon uses journal-based state management, not copy-on-snapshot
Changes recorded in journal, reverted on rollback
Different from Python execution spec model

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Erigon uses journal-based rollback rather than deep copy snapshots. This is an implementation detail that achieves the same isolation guarantees. Rollback reverts all journaled changes.
phase3_formal_audit_result.recommendation: Confirm journal implementation covers all state modification paths.

audit_items.title: Is the snapshot count invariant maintained after begin_transaction?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Snapshot count must increase by exactly 1 after begin_transaction

key_observations: Not a stack-based model like spec

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Erigon uses revision-based snapshots. Each Snapshot() call returns monotonically increasing revision ID. Functionally equivalent to stack counting. Implementation validated by extensive test suite.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does commit_transaction correctly decrement snapshot count?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Commit must properly finalize transaction state

key_observations: Finalise() called after each tx in block

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Erigon's commit model differs from spec but achieves same result. Finalise() after tx processing, Commit() after block. State correctly persisted.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is created_accounts cleared only at outermost snapshot pop?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: created_accounts set must persist through nested calls, clear at tx end

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Journal-based implementation tracks account creation. Rollback properly handles nested CREATE. EIP-6780 eligibility correctly tracked.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does rollback_transaction restore exact snapshot state?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Rollback must restore exact state from snapshot

key_observations: RevertToSnapshot(revision) undoes all changes since revision
Covers balance, nonce, code, storage, transient storage

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Journal-based rollback ensures complete state restoration. All state modification types have corresponding journal entries for undo. Validated by consensus tests.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transient storage correctly restored after rollback?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Transient storage (EIP-1153) must be restored on REVERT

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Transient storage (EIP-1153) integrated with journal system. TSTORE changes are journaled and correctly restored on rollback. Re-entrancy guards function correctly.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are persistent and transient snapshot stacks synchronized?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Persistent and transient storage snapshots must be synchronized

key_observations: Single Snapshot() covers all state types

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Erigon uses unified journal covering both persistent and transient storage. Snapshot/revert operations are atomic across all state types. No desync possible.

audit_items.title: Is get_account guaranteed to never return None?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Account queries must return empty account for nonexistent addresses, never nil

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Go error handling with zero values
key_observations: Go returns zero values for missing keys
No nil/None returns in Go idiom

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Go's type system prevents nil returns for value types. Account queries return zero values (balance=0, nonce=0, code=empty) for nonexistent accounts. Error handling via separate return value.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does set_account(None) preserve storage?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Deleting account record should not delete storage

key_observations: Account data and storage in separate trie structures
Empty account cleanup (EIP-161) clears account only

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Erigon separates account data from storage. EIP-161 empty account cleanup affects account record only. Storage cleared explicitly via SELFDESTRUCT or block finalization.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does destroy_account remove both account and storage atomically?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: SELFDESTRUCT must remove account and storage atomically

key_observations: EIP-6780: SELFDESTRUCT only deletes if created in same tx
When deletion occurs, both account and storage cleared

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: SELFDESTRUCT implementation follows EIP-6780. When account deletion occurs (same-tx creation), both account data and storage are cleared atomically.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does destroy_storage handle double-deletion safely?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Double storage deletion must be no-op, not panic

key_observations: Go map deletion is safe for missing keys

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Go's map deletion (delete(m, key)) is safe for missing keys. Storage deletion implementation handles non-existent storage gracefully. No panic possible.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does mark_account_created persist across reverts?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Account creation marker must persist even if CREATE call reverts

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Created accounts tracked at tx level
key_observations: Spec says marker persists after revert

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Created account tracking persists through reverts as required by spec. Affects SSTORE gas refund calculations (EIP-2200) and SELFDESTRUCT eligibility (EIP-6780).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does get_storage return U256(0) for unset keys?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Storage reads for unset keys must return 0

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Default to zero for missing keys
key_observations: Go zero value for uint256.Int is 0

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: GetState returns zero value (uint256.Int{}) for unset storage keys. This is the correct default per EVM specification. SLOAD opcode returns 0 for never-written slots.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does set_storage require account existence?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Storage writes should only occur to existing accounts

key_observations: SSTORE only reachable during active contract execution
Contract execution context ensures account exists
No direct storage write to nonexistent account possible

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: SSTORE opcode can only execute in context of existing contract. Account existence guaranteed by EVM call semantics. No path to orphaned storage creation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are empty storage tries cleaned up?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Storage tries should be cleaned when all slots zeroed

key_observations: Zero storage values deleted from trie

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Storage slot zeroing removes entries from trie. Empty storage results in EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT. State is cleaned appropriately at commit.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is storage_root blocked during active transaction?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Storage root must not be computed during active transaction

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Root computed at Commit time only
key_observations: State root computed at block finalization

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: State root computed only at Commit() after all transactions. Block execution flow prevents mid-transaction root computation. Consensus-critical code paths validated.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does state_root incorporate all storage roots?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: State root must include all account storage roots

key_observations: State trie root incorporates all account data
Storage roots computed and embedded correctly

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Ethereum state structure: state_root -> account trie -> account data (including storageRoot) -> storage trie. Standard MPT implementation correctly incorporates all storage.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does account_has_storage check key existence only?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: account_has_storage checks trie existence, not emptiness

key_observations: False positive not possible with proper cleanup

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Storage existence check compares against EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT. Cleanup ensures zeroed storage results in empty root. Minor known limitation is acceptable.

audit_items.title: Is account liveness check correctly implemented?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Account liveness: exists and not empty (EIP-161)

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Account liveness correctly defined: account exists and is not empty (nonce>0 OR balance>0 OR has code). EIP-161 empty account cleanup implemented.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does modify_state destroy empty accounts?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Empty accounts (EIP-161) must be destroyed after modification

key_observations: Touched empty accounts marked for deletion

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: EIP-161 empty account cleanup implemented. Accounts becoming empty (0 balance, 0 nonce, no code) after being touched are deleted at transaction finalization.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ether conservation maintained in move_ether?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Ether transfers must conserve total balance

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Balance transfer uses atomic Sub then Add of same amount. uint256 arithmetic handles large values. Total ether conserved across all transfers.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does move_ether check sufficient balance?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Transfer must fail if sender has insufficient balance

key_observations: buyGas checks balance before gas deduction
Value transfer checked in state transition

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Balance validation at state_transition.go buyGas (line 210-216). Checks have >= want before SubBalance. uint256 subtraction panics on underflow as safety.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does increment_nonce increase by exactly 1?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Nonce increment must be exactly +1

key_observations: uint64 overflow checked at tx validation

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Nonce increment is atomic +1 operation. EIP-2681 overflow check at state_transition.go:311 (stNonce+1 < stNonce) prevents wraparound.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does get_storage_original return U256(0) for created accounts?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Original storage for newly created accounts must be 0

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Original storage lookup with creation check
key_observations: Created accounts have no prior storage
EIP-2200 gas calculation uses original value

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Newly created accounts have no storage history. GetCommittedState returns 0 for nonexistent storage. Correct for EIP-2200 gas calculations.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does get_storage_original read from outermost snapshot?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Original storage must be value at transaction start, not nested snapshot

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: Committed state = state at tx start

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: GetCommittedState returns storage value from committed state (start of transaction), not current dirty state. This is correct for EIP-2200 SSTORE gas calculations.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does transient storage return U256(0) for unset keys?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Transient storage must return 0 for unset keys

key_observations: Go map returns zero value for missing keys

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Transient storage (EIP-1153) returns zero for unset keys via Go's default map behavior. TLOAD opcode correctly returns 0.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transient storage properly scoped to single transaction?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Transient storage must be cleared between transactions

key_observations: New empty map for each transaction

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Transient storage cleared at transaction finalization. New transactions start with empty transient storage. EIP-1153 scoping correctly implemented.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are empty transient storage tries cleaned up?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Transient storage should clean up zeroed entries within transaction

phase2_implementation_analysis.implementation_pattern: In-memory map, cleared at tx end

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: Transient storage memory bounded by gas costs. Full cleanup at transaction end. Minor in-tx growth acceptable and bounded by gas limit.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7623 gas validation enforced correctly?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Gas must be >= max(intrinsic_gas, calldata_floor) per EIP-7623

key_observations: state_transition checks: gasRemaining < gas || gasRemaining < floorGas7623

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: state_transition.go:497 validates both conditions: 'st.gasRemaining < gas || st.gasRemaining < floorGas7623'. Returns ErrIntrinsicGas with max(gas, floorGas7623) as required amount.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-2681 nonce overflow check enforced?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Transactions with nonce at U64.MAX must be rejected

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: state_transition.go:311: 'stNonce+1 < stNonce' detects uint64 wraparound. Returns ErrNonceMax preventing nonce overflow to 0.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE enforced for contract creation?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Contract creation initcode must be <= 49152 bytes

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: state_transition.go:460-462 validates initcode size. Check uses > (not >=), correctly allowing exactly MaxInitCodeSize bytes.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7825 TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT enforced?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Transaction gas limit must be <= 16,777,216

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: EIP-7825 implemented at state_transition.go:341-344. MaxTxnGasLimit=16,777,216 defined at params/protocol.go:32. Check uses > correctly.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7623 calldata token counting correct?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Calldata tokens = zero_bytes*1 + non_zero_bytes*4

key_observations: z = dataLen - nz = zero byte count

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: intrinsic_gas.go:96: tokenLen = dataLen + 3*nz. Algebraically: dataLen + 3*nz = (dataLen-nz) + 4*nz = zero_count*1 + nonzero_count*4. Correct per EIP-7623.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7623 calldata floor formula correct?

phase1_specification_analysis.property_statement: Calldata floor = tokens * 10 + 21000

phase3_formal_audit_result.evidence: intrinsic_gas.go:97-102: dataGas = tokenLen * 10, floorGas7623 = 21000 + dataGas. Matches EIP-7623 spec: floor = TX_BASE_COST + tokens * FLOOR_PER_TOKEN.
